tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet during your MSP layover so you're ready to tap through transit the moment you land.
Fill out Visit Japan Web tonight and screenshot the QRs—airport Wi-Fi can be spotty upon arrival.
Hit the Limousine Bus or Keikyu line with your pre-loaded Suica to skip ticket lines after immigration.
If Ichiran is packed, pivot one stop north to Shin-Okubo Koreatown for a midnight KFC and cheese dog feast.
Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast; if it's booked, pivot to Mag's Park rooftop or Shibuya Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby for free crossing views.
If the crew is jet-lagged, swap the late Blue Cave walk for an early nomihodai and call it a night by 23:00.
Arrive at Senso-ji right at 08:30 to beat the mid-morning crowds to the incense burners.
If the Skytree queue is insane, Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room offers the same river view for the price of a beer.
teamLab Planets is already locked in, but if anyone drops out, check Borderless at Azabudai Hills for same-day availability.
Skip Golden Gai's cover charges and hunt for a quiet nightcap at KITTE's rooftop for a free, cinematic view of Tokyo Station.
December brings peak Fuji clarity—if the forecast is clear, consider the FUJI MAXIMALIST swap to Kawaguchiko for the lake-reflection shot.
If the coastal hike taxes your legs, pivot to Enospa onsen in Enoshima to soak with a bay view before the train back.
Run the Airbnb laundry during your farewell dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
Pack first, drink second—bags must close tonight before the Golden Gai encore.
Grab ekiben at Tokyo Station's Matsuri store before boarding—there are 200+ varieties to choose from.
If it rains, swap the Gion walk for the Kyoto International Manga Museum—it's a dangerous, cozy time vortex.
Fushimi Inari at 06:45 is the move; past Yotsutsuji the crowds hit zero for a deserted summit loop.
If it rains, pivot to Sanjusangendo—1,001 golden Kannon statues indoors, criminally underrated.
Skip the Wakakusa-yama climb—it closed for the season on Dec 13, one day before you arrive.
If Kyoto wakes up to snow, override the itinerary: race to Kinkaku-ji at opening for Japan's rarest gold-and-snow photo.
Pre-order your KFC Christmas Bucket well in advance if you want the sacred tradition—lines wrap around the block on the 24th.
If the Nintendo Museum lottery was a bust, lean into Uji with Byodo-in, Tsuen tea, and matcha soba.
Rope-drop Super Nintendo World at 08:30; if Express Passes sold out, use the app timed-entry sprint and single-rider lines.
Non-USJ faction: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan + Tempozan wheel makes for a top-tier alternative Christmas.
This is the longest day of the trip—anyone redlining should skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
If the Peace Museum hits heavy (it will), take a quiet walk through Shukkei-en garden just 10 minutes from the station.
Buy 551 Horai butaman from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner—they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
If 13 days of walking collected their tax, swap the Umeda Sky Building for Spa World's gloriously kitsch Roman baths.
Do a tax-free paperwork check tonight: ensure receipts are with passports and purchases are accessible—customs CAN ask on exit.
On a budget? Kobe-beef bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Zero out your Suica balance at the airport convenience store—transit cards cannot be refunded for cash easily.
Buy Japanese whisky (Hibiki/Yamazaki) AFTER security at HND; keep it sealed for carry-on to avoid checked-bag transfer issues at MSP.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.68, your dollar stretches far—withdraw large lump sums from 7-Eleven ATMs to minimize per-transaction fees rather than making daily small withdrawals.
For a group of 8, skip the taxi queues and stick to transit: load Suica to your phone wallets for instant tap-and-go access without fumbling for paper tickets.
Always carry a small reserve of cash—while major spots take cards, smaller izakayas, Golden Gai bars, and temple entry fees often remain cash-only.
